The test image shows a corn plant with uniformly dried/tan dead leaves throughout the canopy, while surrounding plants are green. The whole plant appears to have wilted and died — no discrete spots, just complete leaf senescence from apparent systemic disease. Tassel is present. This points to a systemic wilt or stalk rot. Top candidates: Goss's Wilt, Stewart's Disease, or a stalk rot.

Let me view a Goss's Wilt reference.

The Goss's Wilt reference shows partial streaking on individual leaves (plant still mostly green), which differs from the test image's complete whole-plant death with uniformly tan/brown dead leaves throughout.

The test image shows: a single corn plant that has completely died (all leaves uniformly tan/dried), tassel present, surrounded by healthy green plants. This complete systemic collapse pattern is most consistent with **Goss's Wilt** in its severe systemic phase — the bacterial infection spreads through the vascular system causing complete plant death. The uniform tan/brown color without discrete spots or lesions, combined with the field context (single plant affected), fits this diagnosis.
